who: Donald M. G. Sutherland, historian of revolutionary France at Maryland, College Park; PhD London 1974.

evidence.says: Identifies Donald M. G. Sutherland as a historian of the French Revolution, Maryland professor, and recipient of a London doctorate in 1974.
The candidate authority names Donald W. Sutherland of the University of Iowa, editor of The Eyre of Northamptonshire.
Iowa identifies Donald Wayne Sutherland as its historian of medieval English law, author of Quo Warranto Proceedings and The Assize of Novel Disseisin.

notes: Reject p-135935: Donald W. Sutherland at Iowa is distinct from Donald M. G. Sutherland at Maryland.

who: Peter H. Smith, Latin American historian at Wisconsin–Madison, 1968–1980; PhD Columbia 1966.

evidence.says: Peter H. Smith’s CV gives a Columbia PhD in 1966 and Wisconsin history appointments from 1968 to 1980; it lists Latin American political change among his fields.
Identifies Peter H. Smith as Peter Hopkinson Smith, with a Columbia doctorate and the book Politics and Beef in Argentina.

notes: The candidate’s Wisconsin employment covers the four AHA dissertations, 1977–1980, and the Latin American field agrees.

who: David Buisseret, historian of cartography and Garrett Professor at Texas, Arlington; PhD Cambridge.

evidence.says: Names David Buisseret as advisor to Alistair Maeer in May 2006 and Jerome Randall Barnes in August 2007, with dissertation titles matching the AHA entries.
Identifies Buisseret as a Cambridge PhD and Texas, Arlington history professor, holding the Garrett professorship in Southwestern studies and cartographic history until retirement in 2006.

notes: Direct matches to two listed students establish the supervisor; the authority agrees in institution and specialization.

who: John Duffy, historian of medicine and public health at Maryland, College Park, later professor emeritus.

evidence.says: Identifies the author of Epidemics in Colonial America as a professor emeritus at Maryland and Tulane, with advanced history degrees from LSU and UCLA.
A 1973 medical-history book review names John Duffy with the affiliation University of Maryland.
The alternative John J. Duffy authority identifies an author of Vermont, an Illustrated History affiliated with Johnson State College, Vermont.

notes: Maryland affiliation and public-health specialization match the AHA dissertations. The John J. Duffy candidate p-107171 is a different scholar.

who: William D. Miller, historian of the Catholic Worker movement who taught at Florida State and Marquette.

evidence.says: Its Marc Ellis biography says he studied at Florida State under William Miller, the historian of the Catholic Worker movement.
The publisher identifies William D. Miller as author of A Harsh and Dreadful Love, his history of the Catholic Worker movement.
The candidate authority identifies William D. Miller, also called William Miller, as a Marquette history professor and author of Memphis during the Progressive Era.

notes: The Florida State teacher is identified through the same distinctive field and authorship as William D. Miller in the candidate authority.

who: History supervisor at Loyola University Chicago for British and Irish dissertations completed in 1969–1971.

evidence.says: James E. O’Neill earned a Chicago history PhD and taught history at Loyola University Chicago before joining the National Archives in 1969.
The candidate James Joseph O’Neill wrote The Nine Years War and a 2013 Queen’s University Belfast doctoral thesis; the authority describes a Cork research fellowship.
Queen’s Belfast records James O’Neill’s doctorate in 2013 and connects it to his 2017 book The Nine Years War.

notes: Reject p-148645: the contemporary Belfast-trained historian is distinct from the earlier Loyola supervisor. The National Archives biography points to James E. O’Neill as the Loyola historian.

who: Rita C-K Chin, historian of modern Europe at Michigan since 2003; PhD Berkeley 1999.

evidence.says: Chin states that she has taught history at Michigan since 2003 and received her Berkeley PhD in 1999.
The authority identifies Rita C-K Chin, author of The Guest Worker Question in Postwar Germany, as a Michigan history professor also listed by the university as Rita Chin.

notes: Authority name variant, institution, employment period and doctorate agree with the AHA supervisor.

who: James A. Epstein, historian of modern Britain at Vanderbilt, 1987–2018; PhD Birmingham 1977.

evidence.says: Vanderbilt records his Birmingham PhD in 1977, teaching there from 1987 to 2018, and authorship of The Lion of Freedom and Radical Expression.
J’Nese Williams’s departmental biography explicitly names James Epstein as her dissertation supervisor.
The authority identifies James A. Epstein, author of The Lion of Freedom, as formerly at Duke and subsequently at Vanderbilt.

notes: Direct student supervision, the Birmingham doctorate, and matching institutional and bibliographic identity confirm the candidate.
